kernel_variant: §3.6 RMSNorm + residual fused fp16 kernel. WG=64 lanes per token, cooperative sum_sq via sub_group_reduce_add. fp16 in/out, fp32 intermediate.

unfused_estimate.model: 2 kernel dispatches (add + RMSNorm), each ~50 us on Adreno, plus intermediate buffer write/read of ~16 KiB at ~50 GB/s = ~0.3 us. Total ~100 us at decode.

lessons: RMSNorm + residual fusion realizes a clean ~2x win at decode hidden=4096. Mechanism: 1 kernel dispatch instead of 2 (saving ~50 us), intermediate add result kept in registers (not written/read through global memory).

Win shrinks as C grows — for C=11008 the kernel is compute-bound, not dispatch-bound, so fusing only saves the one extra dispatch (not the intermediate memory traffic that was anyway small at this scale).

Per-decode-step impact: ~3.5 ms saved across 32 layers from RMSNorm fusion alone. The pattern is now in place for the next fusion candidates (RoPE+QKV+layout transform from paper §3.6 manual fusion, swiglu+matmul, etc.).
Cooperative WG=64 with cl_khr_subgroups + reqd_work_group_size(64,1,1) is now the standard pattern for any kernel that needs a per-token reduce-then-broadcast.
